title: A high-performance speech neuroprosthesis
access_scope: Publisher indexed abstract and PDF methods excerpt; direct HTML redirected to unavailable identity provider.
finding: One participant with ALS; intracortical spiking recordings; 62 words/minute, 23.8% WER with 125000-word vocabulary and 9.1% WER with 50 words. Arrays targeted area 6v and area 44.
limitations: No tonsillar recordings; n=1; speech attempt task. Not an independently proven implanted wireless platform.

title: A high-performance neuroprosthesis for speech decoding and avatar control
access_scope: Author repository article text; publisher indexed abstract; PMC indexed methods passages. Direct PMC hit captcha.
locator: Overview of multimodal speech-decoding system; Neural implant; abstract
finding: One participant with brainstem stroke; 253-channel subdural ECoG surface array, not penetrating single-unit arrays. Attempted silent articulation distinct from imagined speech. Median 78 WPM and 25% WER.
limitations: Correction dated 2024-07-04 inspected through publisher indexed text; use updated anatomical mapping. No tonsillar transfer established.
correction_scope: Publisher indexed correction text inspected: approximately half channels misordered; real-time performance unaffected, anatomical assignments/visualizations corrected.

title: An Accurate and Rapidly Calibrating Speech Neuroprosthesis
access_scope: Full article HTML, targeted Methods, Results and Discussion
locator: Surgical implantation; Results final five Copy Task sessions; Conversation Mode Fig.4; Discussion
finding: One participant, T15, ALS; four 64-electrode arrays (256 sites) in left precentral gyrus. Final five Copy Task sessions WER 2.5% (95% CI 2.0–3.1); selected conversation sessions 3.7% (3.3–4.3), 925 known-label sentences. Total reported use 248.3 hours over 8.4 months.
limitations: Results do not estimate population-level reliability or seven-year durability. Cart, mains power, and percutaneous pedestals; researcher assistance required for connection/start.

title: An instantaneous voice-synthesis neuroprosthesis
access_scope: Publisher indexed abstract, supplementary video 15; PMC indexed participant/result passages; UC Davis author metadata
locator: Abstract; Supplementary Video 15; PMC T15 descriptions
finding: 256 cortical microelectrodes; voice synthesis and prosodic modulation in T15, same participant as Card. Supplementary test reports unintelligible speech reconstructed from residual microphone/stethoscope/IMU signals, unlike cortical signals.
limitations: Continuation of participant evidence, not independent new-patient replication. Residual-biosignal negative control is not a test of proposed pharyngeal implants.

title: Inner speech in motor cortex and implications for speech neuroprostheses
access_scope: Publisher/PMC indexed summary, Fig.7 and methods passages; PubMed and Stanford full author metadata; direct PMC captcha
finding: Four participants with cortical arrays; proof of concept inner speech decoding. T15 among tested participants. Keyword lock in T12: 98.75% detection accuracy; small-vocabulary WER 43.45% reported for that test.
limitations: Neural keyword accuracy is not deterministic consent or zero false activation. Selected task results do not establish unrestricted private-thought reading or tonsillar signal content.

title: Electrode Setup for Electromyography-Based Silent Speech Interfaces: A Pilot Study
access_scope: Publisher/PMC indexed abstract and methods/results passages
finding: Pilot electrode location/type experiments on face/neck EMG; 14 muscles examined in one participant, selecting five face and three neck channels. Frame-based phone classification guides placement.
limitations: Not chronic implanted tonsillar ENG, not inner speech; small electrode-selection pilot does not establish clinical benefit.

title: A streaming brain-to-voice neuroprosthesis to restore naturalistic communication
access_scope: Publisher indexed abstract and PubMed metadata; full publisher HTML unavailable
finding: Streaming speech synthesis using cortical-surface recordings in one participant; abstract reports extension of framework to EMG and single-unit data.
limitations: Methods not fully inspected; framework transfer is not validation of chronic pharyngeal anatomy or performance.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile
authors: National Institute of Standards and Technology
access_scope: Full PDF text accessed; targeted sections 2.2, 2.7, MS-2.2-003, MS-2.5, MS-2.6
locator: Printed pp.6 and 9; sections 2.2 and 2.7; action tables
finding: Confabulated clinical summaries can lead to erroneous diagnoses/treatments; automation bias and data privacy are identified risks. Context-specific evaluations, consent withdrawal and monitoring are recommended.
limitations: Voluntary general AI risk guidance; does not establish incidence of psychiatric misattribution in this proposed device.
